notes: D6-2: the paper presents it as a previously identified hypervelocity white dwarf from Shen et al. (2018); it states that such runaways exceed Galactic escape velocity (T:p21-b6) and that their velocities are high enough that they will likely leave the Milky Way (T:p21-b9), so this is a follow-up rather than a newly found candidate. LP 40-365: the paper supplies this identifier through the plural class name “LP 40-365 stars” (T:p21-b7); under the eponymous-class interpretation, I treat the prototype as part of the paper’s hypervelocity white dwarf population, for which the same escape and likely-leave assessment applies. Figure 13 labels “US 708 (runaway sdB)” (I:p21-b1), but the supplied text does not explicitly establish that it satisfies the Galactic-escape criterion, so it is not included. The unnamed “known/new D6 stars” and “known/new LP−40 stars” plotted in Figure 13 do not identify individual members and are not expanded.

D6-2: D6-2 is identified only in the Figure 13 caption at T:p21-b1, which describes its past/future trajectory and flight time through the supernova remnant G70.0-21.5. The paper does not report an individual right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for D6-2. The velocity range quoted in Section 6.4 is for a broader sample of hypervelocity white dwarfs, not a value specific to D6-2.

LP 40-365: The target LP 40-365 appears only in Section 6.4 (T:p21-b7), where "LP 40-365 stars" is used as a collective label for the slower hypervelocity white dwarfs proposed by Raddi et al. (2019). The paper quotes a general velocity range of ~500 to ~2500 km/s for hypervelocity white dwarfs identified by Raddi et al. (2019) and El-Badry et al. (2023c), which is a sample-level range, not a value for LP 40-365. Figure 13 (I:p21-b1) shows LP 40 stars as a class in the color-magnitude diagram without numeric quantities. No position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, or other star-specific quantity for LP 40-365 is reported, so no quantities are extracted.
